headline: A 2009 executive order kept a set of existing federal advisory committees running instead of letting them expire.
what_it_does: This order extended the life of certain advisory committees that give advice to the President and federal agencies. Under federal law, many of these committees end automatically unless they are renewed. Orders like this one usually renew them for about two more years. The title does not say which committees are covered.

who_it_affects.group: Members of the renewed federal advisory committees
who_it_affects.how: They can keep serving and meeting because their committees were not allowed to expire.

who_it_affects.group: Federal agencies that rely on these committees
who_it_affects.how: They can keep getting outside advice from these groups.

when_it_takes_effect: Signed September 29, 2009; orders of this type usually extend committees for about two years.
